comments.body:
Phase 1 confirmed RCA (rebar-debug).

Proven root cause: test fixtures intentionally operating on bare repositories erase repository-kind intent by routing those commands through generic helpers that encode only `cwd=<bare>` or `git -C <bare>`. Git 2.55 intentionally rejects those implicit-discovery forms under protected `safe.bareRepository=explicit`; it accepts the identical repositories when explicitly selected with top-level `--git-dir`. The changeable artifacts are the bare-repository call sites/helper seams in tests, not the protected Git setting. Generic helpers also serve worktrees, so blanket conversion would regress worktree semantics.

Runtime proof: E1 used one valid ephemeral bare repository with process-only strict config (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `safe.bareRepository=explicit`). Implicit cwd config and `git -C ... symbolic-ref` both returned 128 with the reported errors; changing only targeting to `git --git-dir` returned 0 with exact `false` pin and `refs/heads/tickets` state. Default-config implicit controls returned 0. Invalid ref and nonexistent git-dir remained rc128, ruling out error masking. E2 traced the real fixtures: concurrency invoked `git config gc.autoDetach false` with PWD at remote.git; prepare/reclaim invoked `git -C source.git symbolic-ref ...`; all three errored in fixture setup before product code, while identical default controls passed 3/3. E3 proved mixed-helper dependency: unchanged worktree `-C` succeeded under strict policy, explicitly targeted bare calls preserved all three required pins, and blanket `--git-dir <worktree-path>` failed rc128. This rules out venv/Python, repository validity/ownership, safe.directory, product force/transition/claim code, platform behavior, and protected-config precedence.

Archaeology/safety: commit 07e76a1ce3 and closed bugs ambery-candied-binturong / amicable-unsure-barasinga make all three upkeep pins, `--no-hardlinks`, checked failures, and absence of retry/swallowing load-bearing corruption defenses. Trusted prior art `test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py::_bare_git` from 019e32e03d1 uses explicit `--git-dir` and passes strict policy. Deliberate safe.bareRepository=all uses in the live S3 workflow and reconcile retry tests are distinct contracts and must remain untouched.

Legitimacy: defect. The user explicitly requires supported tests to run locally and in CI; AGENTS.md portability and failure-investigation contracts prohibit dismissing reproducible local failures. Git documents `explicit` as the Git 3.0 default. Existing fixtures contract successful initialization.

Expected repair invariant: commands intentionally operating on a bare test repository identify it explicitly; worktree calls retain existing `-C`/cwd behavior; all command arguments, exact pins/refs/results, `--no-hardlinks`, checked fail-fast behavior, and genuine Git errors remain unchanged. The confirmed construct census spans reported reclaim/concurrency fixtures plus other test-only bare helpers; no production caller is implicated.

trigger_preconditions: real temporary bare repositories; process-only GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL containing safe.bareRepository=explicit; GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; no host/global/system mutation.

test_tier: subprocess integration with real Git repositories and refs; a unit mock cannot exercise Git protected bare-repository discovery.
observable_postcondition: the three actual fixture-backed nodes pass under strict policy and under an isolated default-policy control; exact upkeep pins and HEAD refs remain correct; nonexistent explicit repositories still fail with rc 128.
ci_gate: the held-out integration node is collected by the normal pytest integration/default matrix.
negative_control: identical fixture nodes under isolated default Git config also pass.
collateral_invariants: worktree helper behavior, gc.autoDetach/maintenance.autoDetach/receive.autogc=false, HEAD=refs/heads/tickets, --no-hardlinks, fail-fast subprocess checks, and genuine Git errors remain unchanged.

Final-form held-out oracle was observed RED before repair: 1 failed; its nested real-fixture probe produced exactly three setup errors. Concurrency failed at git config gc.autoDetach false in remote.git (rc 128); prepare-reclaim and reclaim-history failed at git -C source.git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/tickets (rc 128). The test itself was collected and executed, with failure at the strict-policy postcondition rather than import/collection. The oracle has now been removed from the worktree before blind fixing.

comments.body: Held-out GREEN exposed an incomplete repair at the same mechanism in production code: after all fixture-owned implicit bare calls were made explicit, the strict-policy oracle advanced into infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py::_verify_restore and failed at its throwaway restore.git. The script initializes restore.git as bare, then routes fetch and rev-parse through the shared worktree-oriented run_git helper, which uses git -C and is rejected by safe.bareRepository=explicit. This is not a new root cause: it is the construct-sweep sibling previously masked by fixture setup failure. Caller sweep is local: the throwaway repository is owned only inside _verify_restore; normal repo operations elsewhere must remain on run_git. Expected repair: a narrow explicit --git-dir helper for only restored, preserving bundle refs, exact OID comparison, checked failure propagation, and temporary-directory cleanup. File impact expanded to include the script; the held-out oracle was removed again before the continued blind repair.

rebar-debug final repair report (commit 35181363993cddedb0f44c238497b6e5e1b9ee2a).

Problem: bare-repository fixture and restore operations failed under protected safe.bareRepository=explicit.

Proven root cause: commands that intentionally owned bare repositories erased repository-kind intent by invoking generic cwd=<bare> or git -C <bare> helpers. Git therefore treated them as implicit bare discovery and rejected them under explicit policy. Generic helpers also serve worktrees, so blanket conversion was unsafe.

Proof: on identical real repositories, strict implicit config/symbolic-ref/fetch returned 128, top-level --git-dir succeeded, default implicit controls succeeded, and worktree -C remained valid. Runtime tracing identified actual failing helper paths before test bodies. Invalid refs and nonexistent repositories continued to return 128. Archaeology preserved the three upkeep pins, --no-hardlinks, checked fail-fast behavior, and prior corruption defenses.

Test: tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py was final-form RED before repair at all three reported setup paths. After the blind fix it exposed the previously masked production restore.git sibling, remained RED until that same mechanism was repaired, then passed GREEN. Reseeding the exact production defect (--git-dir back to -C) returned RED at the strict restore fetch; restoring the fix returned GREEN. It asserts real strict/default fixture outcomes and a genuine-error control, not private implementation structure.

Fix: introduced narrow bare-only Git helpers using top-level --git-dir at each semantically confirmed test helper call. infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py::_verify_restore now explicitly selects only its owned throwaway restore.git; ordinary repo operations retain shared run_git/-C behavior and exact ReclaimError detail. No Git safety setting changed.

Scope and safety: caller sweep found no caller depending on implicit bare discovery. This restores existing fixture/script behavior, adds no dependency or user-visible capability, introduces no retries/swallowing/skips/xfails, and weakens no assertion. All exact upkeep values, refs, refspecs, OID checks, cleanup, and checked error behavior remain.

Siblings: construct sweep dispositioned all confirmed occurrences across 12 helper-owner test files plus the masked production restore path; deliberate safe.bareRepository=all exceptions in the external workflow and reconcile retry test remain untouched because they serve distinct contracts. Parity census is N/A: this is Git repository-kind targeting, not a multi-surface operation. No residual undispositioned fragility observed.

Replication: full 12-file sibling suite passed 125/125 under isolated strict policy and 125/125 under isolated default policy. Held-out oracle passed; make lint, mypy/typecheck, complexity ratchet, diff-check, commit hooks, DCO, Change-Id, and commit-ticket verification passed.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
Reclaim/concurrency integration fixtures create bare repositories, then invoke Git with the bare repository as `cwd` but without an explicit `--git-dir`. On hosts configured with `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, fixture setup fails before test bodies run:

- `git config gc.autoDetach false` -> `fatal: not in a git directory` (exit 128)
- `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/tickets` -> `fatal: cannot use bare repository ... (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')` (exit 128)

The same errors reproduce from pristine `origin/main`; the failing tests import no force/transition/claim code. Linux CI currently uses Git defaults and therefore does not expose the failure, but the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. Treat agents dismissing reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.

## Safety constraints
Be very cautious about Git configuration. Do not change, unset, or weaken host, global, system, or repository safety settings as remediation. Perform ticket and commit archaeology before proposing a fix so prior bare-repository safety fixes or contracts are not regressed. Prefer explicit, command-scoped repository targeting if the evidence supports it. Do not mask unrelated Git failures.

## Investigation plan
1. Inventory every affected reclaim/concurrency fixture command and the helper/call chain that creates and initializes bare repositories.
2. Search tickets and Git history for prior bare-repository, `safe.bareRepository`, `--git-dir`, fixture, and repository-isolation fixes; record the intended contracts and regression risks.
3. Reproduce from a fresh `origin/main` worktree using isolated command-scoped configuration that sets `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, without mutating host/global Git configuration. Include the default-config run as a negative control.
4. Use runtime evidence to confirm whether implicit repository discovery from a bare-repository `cwd` is the complete mechanism for both failures and rule out venv or product-code explanations.
5. After a proven RCA and legitimacy/caller-dependency checks, design a held-out RED oracle covering both failing command shapes and their observable fixture outcome.
6. Repair only the confirmed mechanism. Evaluate explicit `--git-dir` or an equivalent command-scoped invocation; do not change Git safety settings.
7. Prove GREEN, re-seed the exact defect to prove the oracle returns RED, and rerun the original report under both explicit-safe and default Git configurations.
8. Run focused reclaim/concurrency suites locally and through the normal CI matrix, plus lint/typecheck/complexity gates as applicable. Sweep semantically for sibling bare-repository commands using the same unsafe invocation pattern.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Exact affected fixture commands and call paths are inventoried with citations.
- [ ] Relevant tickets and commits are archaeologically reviewed, with prior contracts and regression risks recorded.
- [ ] The failure is reproduced on pristine `origin/main` using isolated command-scoped `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, without changing host/global Git settings.
- [ ] A default-Git-config negative control demonstrates the environmental trigger while preserving the conclusion that local test portability is a repository responsibility.
- [ ] A runtime-confirmed RCA explains both fixture setup failures and rules out venv and unrelated product-code causes.
- [ ] A held-out final-form oracle is observed RED before the repair and covers both `git config` and `git symbolic-ref` bare-repository initialization paths.
- [ ] The repair explicitly targets the bare repository (for example with `--git-dir`, if archaeology and experiments validate it) and does not weaken any Git safety setting.
- [ ] The held-out oracle is GREEN after repair and returns RED when the exact implicit-discovery defect is reintroduced.
- [ ] Focused reclaim/concurrency tests pass locally under both explicit-safe and default Git configurations and pass in the normal CI matrix.
- [ ] Unrelated Git errors remain visible; no broad exception swallowing, retries, skips, xfails, or test weakening are introduced.
- [ ] A semantic sibling sweep covers other bare-repository fixture invocations and dispositions every confirmed instance.
